scenario: A 70-year-old male presents after a syncopal episode and being found obtunded. He is hypotensive and tachycardic with concern for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm requiring resuscitation, blood products, possible intubation, and urgent transfer for operative management.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start 1 liter normal saline bolus wide open, he's hypotensive at 70/46 and tachy at 130.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Normal saline 1000 mL bolus is up and running.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Sir, you're very sick right now and your blood pressure is dangerously low. I need to know quickly — what symptoms have you been having, and when did they start?

patient_emotion.notes: [clinician: Sir, you're very sick right now and your blood pressure is dangerously low. I need to know quickly — what symptoms have you been having, and when did they start?] fear absent->present: direct disclosure to the symptomatic, unstable patient of serious bad news ('very sick', 'blood pressure dangerously low') is a concrete threat cue raising fear; not extreme because the patient can still be asked to answer and cooperate. sadness stays absent: no actual or anticipated devastating loss framed here. overwhelm stays absent: a single focused question, not a pile of complex findings or simultaneous demands. shame stays absent: no blame, judgment, or exposure.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Cardiac ultrasound back: hyperdynamic LV, no pericardial effusion. Heads up — his GCS just dropped to 8, E2 V2 M4, still hypotensive at 68/46, HR 132, sat 93 on room air.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start norepinephrine, titrate to a MAP of 65. He's still 68/46 after the liter bolus, and echo shows a hyperdynamic LV with no effusion — this is vasodilatory shock, fluid alone won't fix it.

messages.speaker: patient
messages.content: I... felt faint... then passed out. So weak... cold. My side hurts... right here.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me a bedside aortic ultrasound now. 70-year-old with flank pain, syncope, and refractory shock — I need to rule out a ruptured AAA.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Aortic ultrasound back: AAA positive, no intraabdominal free fluid but active bleeding into the retroperitoneum. Norepinephrine is running, still 68/46, HR 135, sat 92 on room air, GCS 8.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: That's a ruptured AAA bleeding into the retroperitoneum — this is hemorrhagic shock, pressors won't fix it. Start 2 units uncrossmatched packed red cells now and activate the massive transfusion protocol. Call vascular surgery emergently, he needs the OR.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Starting massive transfusion protocol, hanging first two units of packed red cells now. I'll keep them coming and monitor for transfusion reaction.

available_results.name: Aortic ultrasound
available_results.result: AAA+, no intraabdominal fluid; bleeding into retroperitoneum.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Add 2 units of plasma now as part of the massive transfusion protocol — he's still 77/50, HR 132 despite red cells and norepi, so I want balanced resuscitation, not just packed cells. Keep vascular surgery moving toward the OR.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Hanging 2 units plasma per massive transfusion protocol now.

available_results.name: Aortic ultrasound
available_results.result: AAA+, no intraabdominal fluid; bleeding into retroperitoneum.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: His GCS is 8 and his airway isn't protected — we're intubating now with RSI, and use reduced-dose induction because he's in hemorrhagic shock. Keep the transfusion running and get vascular surgery moving to the OR.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Airway secured — intubation completed after BVM and RSI meds. Tube's in, patient's on the vent now.

available_results.name: Aortic ultrasound

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Hang 2 more units of packed red cells now, continue the massive transfusion protocol. He's still 70/46, HR 123 with active retroperitoneal bleeding, so keep the products coming. And keep vascular surgery moving to the OR.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Massive transfusion protocol initiated, hanging two units packed red cells now. Blood bank notified for continued product.
